actions.name: conducting hack-and-leak cyber operations
actions.description: Emennet Pasargad conducted hack-and-leak cyber operations involving initial intrusion, theft, and subsequent leak of data, followed by amplification through social media and online forums, and in some cases deployment of destructive encryption malware.

actions.name: executing false-flag campaigns under multiple personas
actions.description: Emennet executed false-flag campaigns under the guise of multiple personas like hacktivist or cyber-criminal groups to avoid attribution.

actions.name: conducting cyber attack against a US-based organization targeting MEK
actions.description: In early 2022, Emennet conducted a cyber attack against a US-based organization as a means to target the Iranian opposition group The People’s Mujahedin (aka MEK), leaking personally identifiable information and causing destructive effects on victim infrastructure.

actions.name: conducting hack-and-leak campaigns involving hacking/theft and information operations
actions.description: Emennet's hack-and-leak campaigns involve a combination of hacking/theft of data and information operations that impact victims via financial losses and reputational damage, including exaggerated or fictitious claims of access or stolen data.

actions.name: choosing victims by conducting online research into leading businesses
actions.description: Emennet chooses victims by conducting online research into leading businesses across several sectors, typically preferring websites running PHP code or those with externally accessible MySQL databases.

actions.name: using open source penetration testing tools such as SQLmap and Acunetix
actions.description: Emennet actors use open source penetration testing tools such as SQLmap and Acunetix to enable their hack-and-leak operations.

actions.name: using website defacements and destructive encryption malware
actions.description: Emennet has used website defacements and destructive encryption malware to cause further harm to victims’ networks.

actions.name: amplifying and promoting theft and leaking of victim data on leak websites, Telegram, and forums
actions.description: Emennet amplifies and promotes the theft and leaking of victim data on their own dedicated leak websites, Telegram, and online hacking and illicit access trading forums, creating social media accounts for each false-flag persona.

actions.name: amplifying information operations through contacting news media and email-marketing services
actions.description: Emennet amplifies information operations through techniques such as contacting news media organizations and using email-marketing services, a tactic previously observed during their campaign against the 2020 US Presidential election.

actions.name: exploiting Log4j vulnerability CVE-2021-44228 to access US organization web server
actions.description: Emennet exploited a Log4j vulnerability CVE-2021-44228 for at least one US-based organization that allowed the actors to access the organization’s web server and used destructive capabilities to take down the web server and associated websites.

actions.name: operating under false-flag persona 'Hackers of Savior' conducting hack-and-leak and defacement campaigns
actions.description: Emennet used the false-flag hacking group persona 'Hackers of Savior' between May 2020 and April 2022, conducting four cyber campaigns targeting entities in Israel involving hack-and-leak activity and website defacements, including a blended campaign of hacking and psychological operations promoting a political narrative.

actions.name: operating under cyber-criminal persona 'Deus' conducting lock-and-leak operation
actions.description: Emennet operated under the cyber-criminal persona 'Deus' in 2021, conducting a lock-and-leak operation targeting an Israeli call service center, encrypting victim computers, leaking company data, and offering to sell the data on public forums and amplifying messaging via a Deus Telegram channel.
